NEW DELHI: Andhra Pradesh Congress president YS Sharmila has shifted her daughter's wedding to another venue after her brother, YS Jagan Mohan Reddy , refused to allow his Bengaluru property to be used for the ceremony.In a social media post on X, Sharmila defended her ownership claim over the Yelahanka property and said it was allotted entirely to her and her children as part of the division of family assets after her brother Jagan Reddy became chief minister.“What is mine is mine, but the greed to covet it is not in my nature. After Jagan Mohan Reddy became chief minister, the Yelahanka property, which until then was a joint family property, came entirely (100 per cent) to my share and that of my children as part of the division of assets. This is the truth, with God as my witness," Sharmila said."Since it is my children's right and the house where my father YSR lived, we wanted to hold my daughter Anjili's wedding there, as she had wished. Ask any household in Telugu society, and they will tell you that getting one's daughter married in one's own house is considered a blessing for every parent," she added.Sharmila said she had decided to organise her daughter's wedding ceremony elsewhere as it was her responsibility to ensure that the event remained free of controversy."However, we are very saddened that we could not fulfil my daughter's wish to have her wedding at the very house where she grew up. My salutations to everyone who felt concerned about my daughter after seeing the developments taking place over the wedding venue," she said."My daughter Anjili's marriage is a match arranged by elders. It is our responsibility to conduct the wedding without controversy and without any disputes. Therefore, we have decided to hold the wedding ceremony of YS Anjili Reddy and Somala Raghuram Reddy at a different venue instead of the Yelahanka house, in the presence of relatives, friends and well-wishers. We wholeheartedly wish that the Telugu people will shower their blessings and good wishes on the couple,” she added.This comes after Jagan Mohan Reddy cited security reasons for refusing to let out the Yelahanka Palace for the wedding ceremony of his niece, Anjili Reddy, in Bengaluru.In the letter, he pointed out that a wedding would bring a large number of guests, caterers, decorators, photographers and other service providers into the residential premises."At the end of the day, this is my home and I want to ensure that my family and I are safe here," Jagan wrote.

Article Title: 490 police personnel awarded home minister's medals, CRPF gets 115 for anti-Naxal operations
Article Text:
CRPF personnel receive 115 Union home minister’s efficiency medals for anti-Naxal operations, including actions in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, as 490 personnel across central and state forces are honoured on Ekta Diwas

NEW DELHI: Central and state police forces personnel who put up a coordinated, decisive fight to eliminate armed Naxalism by March 31, 2026, figure prominently in the list of 490 Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak (Union home minister’s efficiency medal) awardees on Ekta Diwas this year.The two key ‘special operations’ in the Naxal theatre that fetched CRPF personnel 115 home minister’s medals include the second edition of Karreguttalu Hills (KGH-2) action undertaken in February this year and the ‘Operation Medhaburu’ in Jharkhand in January 2026. KGH-2 operation had played a decisive role in crushing the last bastion of CPI(Maoist) on the Chhattisgarh-Telangana border. It led to the surrender of top Naxal leaders Tippiri Thirupati alias Devuji and Malla Raji Reddy alias Sangram, and served as the last nail in the coffin for CPI(Maoist)’s top decision-making bodies, the politburo and central committee. As many as 19 CRPF personnel were honoured on Ekta Diwas, which commemorates the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, for success of the KGH-2 operation.As many as 96 CRPF personnel received the home minister’s medal for a key anti-Maoist operation undertaken in Saranda forests of Jharkhand. It nearly eliminated armed Naxalism in Jharkhand, having led to the killing of central committee member Patiram Manjhi alias Anal Da along with 14 others and forcing politburo member Misir Besra to run for cover; the latter was finally arrested from Dhanbad district in July 2026.The ‘Kendriya Grihmantri Daksha Padak’ — instituted in 2024 — recognises excellence in operations and investigation, exceptional performance, indomitable and daring intelligence service by personnel of the Central and state police forces, besides the meritorious work done by serving govt forensic scientists.While CRPF received the highest haul of home minister’s medals at 115 in the field of special operations, Chhattisgarh police personnel were honoured with 15 medals, Jharkhand police with 28, Telangana police with 21 and Maharashtra police with 7 medals.Other state/UT police honoured for operations include Delhi Police with 36 medals Punjab police with 37, Assam police (19) and Maharashtra police (7).In the investigation field, Central Board for Income-Tax and Customs (CBIC) walked away with 56 medals, CBI with 15, and National Investigation Agency (NIA) and Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) with five medals each. Among the state police honoured for excellence in investigation, are those of Maharashtra, NCT of Delhi, West Bengal, UP, Rajasthan, Bihar, Gujarat, Karnataka etc.In the forensic field, CFSL, Chandigarh was honoured with three medals, while the police in Bihar, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Tamil Nadu received a medal each.
Article Summary: 490 personnel across central and state forces are honoured on Ekta Diwas. CRPF personnel receive 115 Union home minister’s efficiency medals for anti-Naxal operations. Chhattisgarh police personnel were honoured with 15 medals, Jharkhand police with 28, Telangana police with 21 and Maharashtra police with 7 medals.

Article Title: Can high blood sugar help immune cells fight cancer? Study offers new clues
Article Text:
The Journal of Immunology

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Could the same high blood sugar that damages the body also make some immune cells better at fighting cancer? New research offers a surprising clue, finding that high blood sugar enhances the tumour-fighting ability of immune cells in mice, potentially opening a new avenue for cancer treatment.Published in, the study examined why people with type 1 diabetes have been found to have a lower risk of certain cancers, including melanoma, breast and colon cancer. Researchers found that the answer may lie in how high blood sugar changes T cells, immune cells that help the body recognise and attack cancer cells.In experiments, tumours grew more slowly in mice with high blood sugar than in mice with normal blood sugar and diabetic mice whose blood sugar was controlled with insulin. The hyperglycaemic mice also had more T cells, which were more effective at controlling tumour growth.The researchers found that high blood sugar altered a cellular signalling pathway in these immune cells, helping enhance their cancer-fighting activity. When diabetic mice received insulin, their T cells lost this heightened ability, pointing to a possible link between blood sugar levels and immune-cell function.The team then looked for similar changes in humans and found increased activity in the same signalling pathway in immune cells from blood samples of people with high blood sugar. This suggests the mechanism observed in mice may also be relevant to humans, although it does not establish that high blood sugar reduces cancer risk in people.Dr Anamika Bose, assistant professor at the National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research in India and senior author of the study, said the findings could help researchers develop T-cell-based immunotherapies by replicating the immune-cell changes seen in the experiments.The potential lies not in using high blood sugar as a treatment, but in understanding how it changes immune cells and whether those effects can be reproduced safely through targeted therapies.The findings remain preliminary. The tumour experiments were conducted in mice, and further research is needed to determine whether manipulating the same signalling pathway can improve cancer treatment in humans. The study does not suggest that patients should leave diabetes uncontrolled or alter insulin treatment.
Article Summary: High blood sugar changes T cells, immune cells that help the body recognise and attack cancer cells. High blood sugar altered a cellular signalling pathway in these immune cells, helping enhance their cancer-fighting activity. The findings could help researchers develop T-cell-based immunotherapies by replicating the immune-cell changes seen in the experiments.

Article Title: ‘Every case has a story’: Delhi HC judge on why judges are ‘great authors’
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Delhi high court judge Justice Anish Dayal described judges as “great authors” and courtrooms as a “remarkable theatre”, drawing parallels between the judicial process and storytelling.“Judges are great authors. In our case files, we have real stories, real characters, plots, sometimes real, sometimes fictitious. We have problems and, in our judgments, we have resolutions,” PTI quoted Justice Dayal as saying. He made the remarks during his keynote address at the 11th edition of the Himalayan Echoes Festival in Nainital on Friday.“The classic core of a good story is character, problem, and resolution. So, we do it every day, 60-100 cases a day. I guess I am qualified to be here in the literary festival,” he added.Reflecting on his three worlds — the courtroom, literature and the mountains — Justice Dayal said each offered distinct lessons, governed respectively by “rules”, “imagination” and the “uncluttered” force of nature.He noted that nearly 80% of court cases involved ordinary people, whose stories were often hidden behind the “antiseptic language” of case files.“Every single day we read real stories,” he said, highlighting the emotional toll of handling criminal cases and reading accounts of victims' experiences.Justice Dayal described a judge's role as applying “cold, objective reasoning and fairness” while navigating allegations, facts and the law.He also shared amusing examples of mistranslations in court documents. The Hindi expression “mooh boli behan” was once rendered as “mouth spoken sister”, while “somersault” became “the salt that you have in the summer”. Another document used the term “clientess”.“We deal with language in all its corrupted forms and archaic forms also,” he remarked, inviting writers to explore court files for their linguistic curiosities.
Article Summary: Delhi high court judge Justice Anish Dayal described judges as ‘great authors’ He made the remarks during his keynote address at the 11th edition of the Himalayan Echoes Festival in Nainital on Friday. Justice Dayal said each world offered distinct lessons governed by “rules”, “imagination” and the “uncluttered” force of nature.

NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) on Saturday took a dig at the Congress , saying that the party should keep Rahul Gandhi a "mock prime minister for life".Holding a press briefing parallel to the proceedings of the INDIA bloc's "public impeachment" of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra said: "The world has already realised that Rahul Gandhi lacks the fuel. This satellite will never launch. Keep him as your mock Prime Minister for life. We have no objection."Patra said the programme by the Congress-led bloc was "a mockery of the Parliament itself".Tearing into the Congress party, Patra defended the law that lends immunity and protection to CEC Gyanesh Kumar, saying the BJP "did not introduce any law that did not already exist. Immunity and protection for the President and the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) are already enshrined in the Constitution".Patra also cited the August 2023 Telangana lower special court order that directed an FIR to be filed against the Chief Election Commissioner."The high court immediately quashed the order, stating that this was not the correct procedure and directed that it be dismissed. But it became evident then that, due to political pressure, anyone could file a case or an FIR against individuals, even those holding high constitutional offices who are protected by the Constitution, without any regard for the law.Therefore, a procedure was introduced. It was merely a procedure. The legal provision already existed within the Constitution. The Constitution of India provides this protection," he said.BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad slammed Rahul Gandhi for making "a mockery of the people of the country" and dared him to resign."These individuals do not participate in parliamentary discussions; instead, they are making a mockery of the people of the country... Nehru ji became Prime Minister by stealing votes... How long will you continue to ridicule constitutional institutions? When a decision goes in your favor, the Election Commission seems 'fine' to you... This is shameful. I challenge Rahul Gandhi—if you have the courage, you should resign," the BJP leader told news agency ANI.Addressing a press brief, BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra said: "If there was ever a vote theft in India, it was committed by the first member of the Gandhi family, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru, who stole the votes of prominent Congress leaders. Those leaders had cast their votes in a ballot box to elect Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel as Prime Minister. By stealing those votes, Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru became the Prime Minister of the country, an unelected Prime Minister. "Patra, who is MP from Puri Lok Sabha constituency, called the "mock parliament" a "drama", and highlighted that the Speical Intensive Revision (SIR) was ongoing and substantiated the claims around the "13 crore delted voters"."Across various states, the names of 13 crore people have not yet been included in the final electoral roll. Why is this the case? What is this 'ASDD' formula? 'A' stands for 'Absent'. There is an official known as a BLO (Booth Level Officer). The BLO is responsible for an 'enumeration form' that every individual is required to complete. The BLO visits your home three times with this form. If you are not present on any of these three occasions, you are marked as 'absent', and your name is excluded from the electoral roll. What about 'S' in 'ASDD'? It stands for 'Shifted'—permanently shifted," Patra said.Earlier, Union home minister Amit Shah slammed Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav for raising the issue of voter irregularities ahead of the INDIA bloc's Delhi Chalo march and challenged them to discuss the issue during a special session of Parliament.While addressing a gathering in Uttar Pradesh's Lucknow, Shah highlighted the BJP's electoral victories in states like Haryana, Maharashtra and Bihar, and said that the opposition had realised that it could not win elections."In Haryana, the Bharatiya Janata Party formed the government after securing the highest number of seats. In Maharashtra, the NDA formed the government with the largest share of seats. In Bihar, for the first time, a chief minister from the Bharatiya Janata Party took office. In Delhi, the Bharatiya Janata Party formed the government after three decades. In Puducherry, the Bharatiya Janata Party formed the government once again. In Assam, we achieved a hat-trick by winning 100 seats, and in Bengal, we completely wiped out Mamata Didi," Shah said."After the events in Bengal, they have realised that they simply cannot win elections," he added.The Union home minister said that "Rahul Baba" and Akhilesh were cut from different cloth and accused them of "blaming the umpire" instead of accepting defeat."Naturally, when a team loses a match or a game, they should sit down and practise more - that is what is expected, isn't it? But 'Rahul Baba' is cut from a different cloth. The same goes for Akhilesh and others in the 'INDIA' alliance who are with him. Instead of accepting defeat, they began accusing the umpire of cheating, claiming that votes were stolen," Shah said.He further said that the opposition had no intention of raising the issue in Parliament and accused it of refusing to let the House function."Rahul Baba, I challenge both you and Akhilesh Yadav right here and now: the Bharatiya Janata Party is fully prepared to discuss this in Parliament. We have nothing to hide. Let us convene a special session of Parliament - but they have no intention of speaking there. They refuse to let Parliament function; instead, they just create a ruckus," Shah said.The INDIA bloc on Saturday demanded the removal of Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of being part of a "devious and malevolent criminal conspiracy orchestrated by the BJP to steal national and state elections". The opposition alliance also demanded that he be tried for "treason" in a court.The allegations were outlined in a resolution read out by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge during a symbolic "public impeachment" programme against Kumar. The CEC has faced sustained criticism from opposition parties over alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The resolution said that Members of Parliament belonging to the INDIA bloc had resolved to seek Kumar's impeachment on the basis of the charges listed in the document.The first charge accused Kumar of overseeing and participating in a "devious and malevolent criminal conspiracy orchestrated by the BJP to steal national and state elections".

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan continued his remarkable run in T20I cricket, rewriting the Indian record books with an impressive half-century in the fifth and final match against New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Sunday. The left-handed batter surpassed Suryakumar Yadav 's record for most runs by an Indian in a calendar year in T20Is, while also completing 2,000 runs in the format.Kishan brought up the landmark with an aggressive 61 off just 32 balls, featuring five sixes and as many fours. He now has 1,220 runs in 37 matches and innings in 2026, surpassing Suryakumar's previous record of 1,164 runs, which he had accumulated in 2022.Kishan has been in outstanding form throughout the year, averaging 35.88 at a strike rate of 171.58. His tally includes a century and eight half-centuries, underlining his consistency and attacking approach in the shortest format.The 28-year-old also became the seventh Indian to cross 2,000 runs in T20Is, reaching the milestone in his 69th innings. He is the third-fastest Indian to achieve the feat in terms of balls faced, having taken just 1,345 deliveries to get there.Only Abhishek Sharma (1,024 balls) and Suryakumar Yadav (1,164 balls) have reached 2,000 T20I runs quicker in terms of deliveries among Indian batters.Suryakumar had set the benchmark in 2022 with 1,164 runs in 31 matches at an average of 46.56 and a strike rate of 187.43. Kishan went past that mark with his latest innings, taking his 2026 tally to 1,220 runs.His prolific year has also been fuelled by his contribution to India's title-winning campaign at the ICC Men's T20 World Cup, where he scored 317 runs. The wicketkeeper-batter has carried that form into the bilateral assignments, establishing himself as one of India's most productive performers in the format.Kishan's 2,000-run milestone also puts him in an elite group of Indian T20I batters. He has scored 2,016 runs in 69 matches, with 206 fours and 96 sixes.In terms of innings taken to reach 2,000 runs, Virat Kohli and Suryakumar lead the Indian list, having achieved the feat in 56 innings each. KL Rahul reached the landmark in 58 innings, while Abhishek Sharma took 64. Kishan completed it in his 69th innings to occupy fifth place on that list.Kishan's record-breaking knock came at a crucial stage after India suffered an early collapse. Asked to bat first after New Zealand won the toss, the visitors struck early, with Adam Milne dismissing Abhishek Sharma in the second over.Kishan, coming in at number three, responded with an attacking approach and joined Shreyas Iyer in rebuilding the innings. The pair added 107 runs for the third wicket in little more than seven overs, giving India the momentum after the early setbacks.Kishan initially took time to settle before shifting gears, while Iyer was aggressive from the outset. The India batter struck four sixes and three fours during his 50 off 23 deliveries, registering another valuable contribution in the middle order.Kishan brought up his half-century off 28 balls with a six off Michael Bracewell. Iyer soon followed, reaching his fifty in 22 deliveries.New Zealand, however, fought back by removing both set batters in quick succession. Blair Tickner dismissed Kishan, who was caught at deep mid-wicket, before Iyer fell to Adam Milne.Naman Dhir added 33 off 23 balls, while Nitish Kumar Reddy contributed 22 off 17 deliveries as India finished with 191/8.India had already secured an unassailable 3-1 lead in the five-match series heading into the final encounter.
Article Summary: Ishan Kishan becomes the seventh Indian to reach 2,000 runs in T20Is. The 28-year-old is the third-fastest Indian to achieve the feat in terms of balls faced, having taken just 1,345 deliveries to get there. He also overtakes Suryakumar Yadav's record for most runs by an Indian in a calendar year.

Article Title: Karnataka woman pays Rs 1.99 lakh to wedding photographer who promised personal coverage, finds assistants covering ceremonies instead; consumer court orders Rs 35,000 compensation and litigation expe
Article Text:

BENGALURU: A wedding photographer in Karnataka has been directed to pay Rs 35,000 in compensation and litigation expenses to a bride after a consumer court found deficiency in service over his failure to personally cover her wedding despite an alleged promise to do so, according to report by Bar and Bench.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Hassan held that replacing a specifically engaged photographer with assistants without informing the client or obtaining her consent amounted to a breach of contract under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.According to a report by Bar and Bench, the order was passed on October 17 by a bench comprising Commission president Chanchala CM and member Anupama R in a complaint filed by Chinmayi M against Karthik Singh, proprietor of Karthik Singh Photography and his associate Sharvari.Chinmayi had hired Singh after viewing his Instagram portfolio, which showcased his photography and videography work. The parties agreed on a package worth Rs 2.05 lakh, covering candid and cinematic videography for the engagement and other wedding-related ceremonies. She paid Rs 1,99,200, including Rs 16,200 towards travel expenses.According to the complaint, Singh had assured her that he would personally photograph important ceremonies, including the engagement, wedding reception and wedding.However, he allegedly sent other photographers without informing her.The bride alleged that the team arrived 70 minutes late and missed several important moments, including rituals at her home, the bridal procession accompanied by relatives and musicians, and the groom's arrival in a car.She further alleged that the photographers later asked the family to recreate some of the missed moments artificially.The complaint also raised concerns over poorly edited videos, missing footage, the absence of drone coverage, the placement of an LED screen and delays of nearly a year in delivering the photographs, videos and wedding album.Singh denied the allegations, maintaining that the photographers were part of his regular professional team and worked under his supervision. He argued that the complainant had failed to establish any technical deficiencies in the work and was attempting to avoid paying an outstanding amount of Rs 22,000.The Commission, however, found that Singh had failed to honour his commitment to personally photograph the ceremonies. It also observed that clients engage professionals based on their individual skills and expertise, making their identity an important consideration in such contracts."In professional contracts involving creative or specialized skills like photography, medical procedures, or legal representation the identity and unique talent of the service provider are often the primary reason for the contract. Substituting that person with an assistant without the client's consent constitutes a direct breach of contract," it said, as quoted by Bar and Bench.The Commission said photographers must inform clients if they are unable to attend an event, giving them an opportunity to make alternative arrangements.It relied on WhatsApp conversations to establish that the photographer's assistants had arrived 70 minutes late, resulting in important wedding rituals being missed.However, the Commission rejected the allegations concerning the poor quality of photographs and the absence of drone coverage.It directed Singh and his associate to pay Rs 25,000 as compensation and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses. The amount must be paid within 45 days of the order, failing which it will attract annual interest of 10% until payment.
Article Summary: A bride in Karnataka has been directed to pay Rs 35,000 in compensation and litigation expenses to a wedding photographer. A consumer court found deficiency in service over his failure to personally cover her wedding despite an alleged promise to do so. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Hassan held that replacing a specifically engaged photographer with assistants without informing the client amounted to a breach of contract.

That’s the Delaware connection. According to AeroCorner, the aircraft is based in Wilmington, Delaware, just 10 minutes from Philadelphia International. AeroCorner estimates the aircraft at $12.2 million.Swiss aircraft company Pilatus manufactures the PC-24. It is called a Super Versatile Jet because it has a dual role: business-aviation comfort and short-runway performance.Two William FJ44-series turbofan engines power the jet. It has a thrust rating of 3433 pounds. Its takeoff distance is 3,090 ft. The PC-24’s maximum speed is 440 knots and a maximum range of 2,000 nautical miles with six passengers. It can operate from unpaved runways, including grass, gravel, earth, paved strips, and snow-covered surfaces.Its landing gear and design let it access smaller airports unsuitable for larger business jets. Inside, it boasts a spacious cabin, flat floor, and a large cargo door. It’s ideal for business travel and journeys that involve carrying extra baggage.In February 2024, after Super Bowl LVIII in Las Vegas, Jason Kelce was spotted leaving Harry Reid International Airport through the commercial terminal. Barstool Sports reported that Kelce chose commercial travel even though most wealthy attendees at the Las Vegas championship game preferred to fly via private aircrafts.He earned widespread praise from fans as a “man of the people.” The report noted that over 500 private jets had left the city, but Jason was photographed flying commercially. The commercial flight travel took place reportedly before the Pilatus PC-24 registration date.The reported super versatile jet was registered in November 2024. The Pilatus PC-24 is owned by “KELCE AIR LLC.”An article published by Tim de Vries of AeroCorner also points out that the only Kelce brother associated with an aircraft registered through Kelce Air LLC is Jason. Travis Kelce reportedly doesn’t own an aircraft, he charters and flies as a passenger, as per AeroCorner.Or maybe this N620JK belongs to all the Kelces. But if it were Travis’, then wouldn’t it be N870TK? Just speculating. His billionaire pop superstar wife, Taylor Swift , owns a reported $54 million Dassault Falcon 7X private jet registered as N621MM. Maybe he doesn’t need one. So the Pilates aircraft could be Jason’s. Stressing the word “could.”
Article Summary: Jason Kelce reportedly owns a Pilatus PC-24 Super Versatile Jet. The aircraft has nine seats, two Williams FJ44-series engines, and weighs less than 12,500 pounds. The registered owner is listed as Kelce Air LLC, a Delaware-based limited liability company.

Article Title: From asses to masses, Republicans wonder if Trump can still deliver wins
Article Text:
MAGA boss is getting huffy about the physical toll.

TOI Correspondent from Washington:

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think Trump's approach to campaigning is effective? Yes, it resonates with his supporters No, it's damaging his image Not sure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

US President Donald Trump has spent an extraordinary amount of campaign time discussing the physique of other public figures, including their butts, legs, and other physical attributes. While the Republican Party supremo may be preoccupied with posteriors and treating his MAGA masses to jokes about asses, GOP candidates have a rather more pressing anatomical question: does Trump still have legs to carry them over the line in the midterms elections?Indeed, the MAGA boss is getting huffy about the physical toll and relentless schedule of the campaign trail and is now approaching it with the enthusiasm of a man who has just been informed that his prison sentence has been extended. "I thought this was going to be my last one. I thought I could relax. Twenty-eight days in a row of this crap is a lot. My voice is operating at about 49.2%," he grumbled at a rally in Florida on Friday, complaining, "So on Sunday, while you're all watching football, I'll be traveling in a very beautiful airplane to Iowa, to Kansas. "It takes a peculiar sense of self-deprecation to describe one’s own rallies as “crap,” but this is Trump.At another rally last month, he offered an astonishingly candid description of his relationship with his followers, saying, "I could say the stupidest thing, and y'all would just laugh and clap." The question political pundits are trying to figure out is at what point does his MAGA faithful wake up to being told the rallies they flock to are “crap,” and they are possibly stupid. Right now, there is little evidence they have abandoned their leader in large numbers, although there are signs the sheen is wearing off.At a Trump rally in South Carolina last week, a man approached by Fox News was asked the perfectly innocuous question: Why are you here? "Well, in the late 70s, I was a little too young to go to South America for the Jonestown Massacre. But this is as close as I'll ever get…There's nothing like seeing a cult right up front," he said. The reference was to the 1978 incident in Guyana, when more than 900 followers of cult leader Jim Jones died in a mass murder-suicide episode unparalleled in modern history. The reporter, who had assumed the man, a former Republican, was a Trump supporter, bolted in embarrassment to find someone else to interview.Invoking the Jim Jones cult was an unusually savage description of MAGA faithful, but it also captured a question increasingly confronting Republicans as America heads to polling stations on Tuesday: Is Trump's political movement still an electoral coalition, or has it become a congregation whose members would applaud even if the pastor preaches violence?Yet this is the peculiar political chemistry of MAGA; Trump knows his audience, and his audience knows him. Their relationship is not necessarily built on policy consistency, intellectual coherence or even conventional political expectations; It is built on identity, grievance, resentment and an enduring conviction that Trump, however outrageous, is fighting their battles despite stories of grift and corruption Washington is now awash with.There is also a generational divide that is becoming increasingly visible. At rallies and in interviews, parents and children sometimes find themselves on opposite sides of the Trump phenomenon. Younger family members challenge the president's rhetoric and politics, while their parents remain devoted supporters. Trump has repeatedly turned this domestic disagreement into a campaign punchline, telling younger people, in effect, that their parents vote for him. It is a useful reminder that MAGA is not simply a political preference; For many, it has become an identity, strong enough to survive Thanksgiving dinner, family arguments, and interventions by offsprings armed with a smartphone and fact-check.The generational friction has also become lucrative entertainment for many liberal podcasters and social-media influencers who have discovered that interviewing committed Trump supporters, asking seemingly straightforward questions, and allowing the answers to speak for themselves can generate enormous online engagement. The format is simple: find a MAGA dope, ask about a policy, a political contradiction or an extraordinary presidential statement, and let the conversation unfold. The audience is invited to laugh, cringe or marvel because interviewee often appears oblivious to the fact that the exchange is being consumed as comedy rather than political persuasion. Vivek Ramaswamy , the Indian-American Republican gubernatorial hopeful in Ohio, recently discovered how easily these encounters can be weaponised. During an interaction, a man confronted him with a question about why a pedophile appeared in one of his campaign advertisements. Ramaswamy initially looked bewildered, attempted to respond and eventually walked away as the exchange circulated online. Whether it is a carefully staged prank or an opportunistic ambush, the point is that Republican politicians are increasingly encountering an opposition that understands the economics of viral embarrassment.And Trump himself continues to supply the material. The president's own rallies have become an increasingly unpredictable mixture of political campaigning, stand-up comedy, grievance therapy -- and occasionally, an anatomy lecture even as his party’s ass is on line come November 3.
Article Summary: President Donald Trump has spent an extraordinary amount of campaign time discussing the physique of other public figures, including their butts, legs, and other physical attributes. GOP candidates have a rather more pressing anatomical question: does Trump still have legs to carry them over the line in the midterms elections?

Article Title: 'WTC win was no fluke': Temba Bavuma slams 'critics' after statement win over Australia
Article Text:
South Africa's captain Temba Bavuma celebrates after hitting a century on day three of the second cricket test match between South Africa and Australia, in Gqeberha, South Africa. AP/PTI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

South Africa captain Temba Bavuma believes his team have answered questions about their World Test Championship (WTC) triumph after completing a 2-1 series win over Australia. The Proteas came back from a defeat in the opening Test to win the next two matches, including the series decider by 176 runs at Newlands on Saturday.South Africa's recent run includes qualifying for the 2025 WTC final even after forfeiting a series in New Zealand, beating defending champions Australia in the final at Lord's, drawing a series in Pakistan and winning a Test series in India for the first time in 25 years. They have now added a home series victory over Australia to that record.The win in Cape Town also took South Africa to the top of the ICC Test rankings. Simon Harmer played a key role in the victory, taking 6/16 in the second innings and finishing with match figures of 10/120. Kagiso Rabada claimed three early wickets as Australia were bowled out for 111 while chasing 288.South Africa's series win came after they lost the opening Test in Durban by 214 runs. They responded with an innings-and-31-run victory in Gqeberha before sealing the series in Cape Town.Speaking after the win, Bavuma reflected on the demands of the series and the effort required from his players to maintain their performance."It's tough, to be honest," he said. "You wake up every day asking yourself to be at your best.Physically, there's times where you feel like you can't go at 100%, but you need to dig deep, and if the opportunity's there, make sure you're in the best mental space to make the play for the team. Even if things don't go well for you with the ball or the bat, you still need to be looking at ways as to how you can contribute within the team. "Bavuma described the series as "15 days of just pressure". It came after South Africa had gone almost a year without playing a Test and 21 months without playing one at home. He said the opening defeat in Durban had been a "rude awakening"."There were two quality sides who came up against each other, and really forced each other to play their best cricket," Bavuma said. "It will be important for us to acknowledge what we've achieved, celebrate whatever milestones, take whatever learnings that come with it, and really bask in what we've achieved. In the two-and-a-half years, if you look at the team, we've been able to squeeze out every inch of every individual.Bavuma also hopes the team's performances will change how they are viewed by critics, who have questioned whether their WTC title was a one-off achievement."I do hope with the way that we've performed, not the result, but the way that we've performed, it's given that belief. And I guess in a cheeky way, answer to certain critics saying that what we did at the WTC was a fluke. The sky's the limit for the team."

Proteas came back from a defeat in the opening Test to win the next two matches, including the series decider by 176 runs at Newlands on Saturday. South Africa's recent run includes qualifying for the 2025 WTC final even after forfeiting a series in New Zealand.

Article Text:

TimesofIndia.com

Manisha, what was going through your mind during the final? You were trailing, and then suddenly you took the lead. What did you do to turn things around? There are times in such situations when things can go either way.

Manisha, there is a shooter from Jind named Neeru Dhanda. You must have heard of her?

NEW DELHI: “Bhai saab, Jind Pandavon ki nagari hai, kuch to baat to hogi [Jind is the land of the Pandavas. There must be something special about it]”Manisha Bhanwala said these words with a smile a day after creating history at the World Wrestling Championships on Friday. The wrestler from Jind, Haryana, had just become the first Indian woman to win a gold medal at the World Championships.Perhaps there is something special about this town - Jind. Manisha is not the only athlete from Jind to make the country proud this year.Exactly a month earlier, another daughter of the town, Neeru Dhanda, won gold in trap shooting at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya. She became the first Indian woman to win an individual Asian Games gold medal in trap shooting.Jind has a deep connection with the stories of the Mahabharata. According to local belief, the Pandavas built a temple dedicated to Goddess Jainti Devi before going to war against the Kauravas. They prayed to the goddess and sought her blessings for victory. The town was originally known as Jaintapuri, meaning the abode of Goddess Jainti Devi. Over time, the name became Jind.And now, Manisha has added another proud chapter to the story of this town.But for the 59kg wrestler, the biggest moment of her life was also a deeply personal one.When she won the gold medal, she did not celebrate alone. She kept the medal and a photograph of her late father beside her pillow. She made a video call to her mother and brother before going to sleep. Before kissing her father's photograph, she had one more moment with the man whose memories and teachings continue to guide her.Her father may not have been there to witness her historic achievement, but Manisha made sure he was part of it.The wrestler has often spoken about the lessons she learnt from the Bhagavad Gita through her father. She believes in the principle of karma - doing one's duty and leaving the result to God. She follows it in her life and carries the same belief onto the wrestling mat.That belief was tested in the World Championships final in Astana, Kazakhstan. Manisha was trailing American wrestler Abigail Nette by six points in the women's 59kg final. But she refused to give up. She fought back brilliantly to win 8-6 and claim the gold medal.With this victory, Manisha became the first Indian woman to win a World Championships gold medal in wrestling. She is only the second Indian overall to achieve the feat, after the legendary Sushil Kumar, who won the men's 66kg title in 2010.spoke to Manisha from Astana about her thrilling comeback in the final, her celebration with a T-shirt carrying her father's photograph, Iranian-style wrestling, her belief in karma and her dream of winning gold at the Los Angeles Olympics.I was trailing. When I went to the starting point, I felt that only one point had been scored, so why were they giving that opportunity at that moment? Even then, I challenged the decision, but they still awarded the points. I objected, but my challenge was rejected. Even after that, I felt that I would be able to do it. I had that feeling.I hadn't had a good Asian Games. I was getting very frustrated. Doubts were also coming into my mind. Was I doing something wrong? This was something I asked myself when I closed my eyes for a few seconds. Was my practice wrong? Many things were going through my mind, but I believed that I could do it. I felt it from within that I could turn things around. And I did.Yes. I faced the same situation at the 2025 Asian Championships. I was losing, but I made a comeback and won the bout.My style of wrestling is different from that of other girls. I wrestle somewhat like the Iranian style. The way I am trained is also different. For the last five years, the focus has been on being able to do anything in the first three minutes. But after that, it is about maintaining patience, stamina and strength. I also work on keeping myself mentally strong and excited. I work on all these things.If you dominate the first two to three minutes, the bout is yours. After that, it is all about your patience and analysis of the opponent. If you are trailing, you will try to score, and in most cases, you lose patience and focus, and eventually the match too.To develop that kind of strength, like Iranian wrestlers have, a lot of force is required. I am a little shorter in comparison, so I have to work harder. First, I practise with boys. If I get injured, I may have to stay away for two days. So I try to do everything I can. Even if I have pain anywhere in my body, I complete my recovery. I spend my entire day on recovery, and only after that do I go back. I take care of my body as much as I can.I train with multiple partners, including boys. They help me generate more force. After the selection or during camps, when it becomes clear which wrestlers will be going, we practise with those who are selected. My coach and I tell them what needs to be done and what kind of practice is required. We make a particular plan and follow it.My father sahab. My entire life is dedicated to my father sahab. He was such a lovely soul. He was not literate. He never went to school, but always supported me throughout my journey. There were taunts like, 'Ladki hai, padha likha le, shaadi kar de.' But he never listened to them. Such was my father.I am what I am today because of him. I miss him a lot. But I still feel he is always sitting beside me. He is always there to clap for me, motivate me and cheer for me whenever I hit the mat. I feel he is always around.You took out that T-shirt with your father's photograph after winning the gold medal.As I said, he is everything to me. He was a farmer who used to plough the fields himself. We didn't have much money. But I never got to know how he fulfilled all my needs.My father was a farmer. He used to work in the fields and operate the plough. He knew nothing about sports or anything like that. He was a farmer who never treated me differently because I was a girl. He never put any pressure on me about what I was doing or what I was eating.Even today, I feel that kind of support is rare. Despite never going to school and not being able to read or write, he was an open-minded person. He was a lovely soul. He was very particular about his work. From childhood, he taught me what karma means. He taught me the right things at that time.Our family was not financially well-off. We were very poor. We did not even have land of our own. He followed the Gita and always asked me to follow it too.Absolutely not. He never let me feel that I was missing anything. Let me tell you something. Even today, I don't know how my father managed everything. He worked day and night.When I started wrestling in 2015, I needed wrestling shoes. I just said once, 'Papa, wrestling ke shoes chahiye.' He kept his hand on my head with a smile and said, 'Haan, ho jayega, dikkat koi nahi hai.' He gave me shoes worth Rs 7,000 within a couple of days. Those were very expensive at that time.But from the very first day, he always made sure I got good things. He never let me feel that I was missing anything. I never asked him how he got those things, and he never told me.When I went to school, my teachers would ask me what my father did. When I told them that he was a farmer, they would sometimes find it difficult to believe that my father was a farmer.In 2022, when I was selected for my first championship, my father was very excited. I had beaten Sakshi Malik three times. I was doing really well. I had also defeated Sangeeta Phogat.My father started getting excited when he saw his dream beginning to come true. He was completely fine that night when I got selected for the Asian Championship. In the afternoon, he was told to go and sleep. He didn't wake up after that. He died of a heart attack. It had been eight years since then, and that very night, I had a flight for the championship.I don't know. I was numb. I lost the person whom I loved more than anything in this world. And that person was no longer with me. That night... I don't know how to explain it. It was tough to ask myself whether I should hold on to the feeling that my father was still with me.I had a flight to the Asian Championships that same night. I just sat in a corner. After the cremation, my mother said, 'Apne papa ka dream tu poora nahi karegi toh kaun karega?' She said, 'Kya karegi aise baith ke, chal jaa, competition ladd.'I reached Mongolia from India. I did not even realise how I had travelled or how I had reached there. I don't remember that day properly. I don't remember where I was going, what day it was or what was happening around me. When I returned to my room after winning bronze, I broke down.My mother, my brother, my sister-in-law and my nephew.My brother used to beat me up a lot when we were children. He used to fight with me. I was small, so I used to get beaten up and cry. My father sahab used to beat him. My father sahab said, 'Tu strong bann, pehelwaan ban, isko pitiyo bade hoke.'That's how I decided to become a wrestler.My brother also left kabaddi midway for me. He said that I should continue and that we would both do it together. He now stays at home and takes care of whatever work needs to be done. He looks after the farming. We also have a medical store there, which he manages.I am from Jind. I have been living in a village in Rohtak for the last 10 years. I live on rent. I have no idea how my family manages those expenses too. My father sahab and mother never told me. They always said, 'Apne khel pe dhyan do.'Olympic gold. I will do that for my father sahab. I am confident about that. Wrestling and winning gold are the two things that remain in my life. Apne father sahab ko samarpit hai dono ab.He always used to say, 'Beta Olympics medal jitenge ek din.' Whenever he asked, I used to reply, 'Pitaji, Olympics medal nahi, Olympics gold.'Yes. I know her. She is from Jind itself. She won gold at the Asian Games. Jind is the land of the Pandavas. Kuch toh baat hai iski hawa mein.My father sahab was a follower of the Gita and believed in karma. He taught me to keep doing my karma. Just keep doing your work. Only God knows what you are going to receive and what you are going to get. In reality, you receive what you work for.
Article Summary: Manisha Bhanwala is the first Indian woman to win a gold medal at the World Championships. The 59kg wrestler from Jind, Haryana, was trailing American Abigail Nette by six points in the women's final. She fought back brilliantly to claim the 86 and claim the gold medal.

Arizona Cardinals 30-year-old safety Budda Baker has become one of the most popular names circulating in the NFL trade discussions - back in the 2026 offseason and even now in the midseason.The eight-time Pro Bowler re-entered the trade discussion because the trade deadline is here - November 10 and because he addressed fresh questions about his trade rumors while wearing a creepy, scary Halloween clown mask during his latest media availability.The veteran defensive back’s three-year, $54 million contract makes him an unrestricted free agent in 2028; 2027 is his final year, which is why he’s a trade subject. So far, two teams have emerged as potential landing spots for the Washington alum: the Buffalo Bills and the Jacksonville Jaguars.Budda Baker’s trade rumors took a swift turn in his recent press conference, when reporters asked him about the growing speculation.Wearing a traditional Halloween costume and conveniently hiding his true feelings, the 30-year-old safety said his entire focus is on Arizona’s next matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on November 1, 2026, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.“My approach is I’m here. I want to win. I want to be here. And I’m just controlling what I can control, just taking it one week at a time, and hopefully when the deadline ends, I’ll still be here. If not, I mean, it’s a business.I understand at the end of the day and that’s it. So, at the end of the day, I’m here, be where your feet are. I’m happy to be a Cardinal and just focus on getting a W this week vs. Cowboys,” he said, shaking that scary costume with every sentence.According to ESPN, Baker has not requested a trade or asked the Cardinals to keep him. He expressed the desire to stay with the team. He understands the business side of professional football, but he has not specifically discussed his future with Arizona GM Monti Ossenfort. Josh Allen ’s team, the Buffalo Bills, have become a potential landing spot for Budda Baker because the Arizona Cardinals safety could strengthen their secondary.According to Bleacher Report, the Arizona Cardinals veteran is among Buffalo’s top 10 realistic trade candidates. Baker’s vast experience, versatility, and ability to contribute near the line of scrimmage speak volumes about what he can offer the Bills.In exchange, Buffalo could send a 2027 fourth-round pick, as per Bleacher Report’s Brad Gagnon. While Bleacher Report’s Alex Kay suggests a 2027 third-round pick as acquisition cost for Baker. However, financial considerations could complicate the matter.According to Spotrac, Baker is scheduled to earn a $14.41 million base salary, a $1 million roster bonus, and a $500,000 workout bonus in 2026. He carries a $19.21 million cap hit and a $22.03 million dead cap value.Budda Baker is owed $16.2 million in 2026 and $17.8 million in 2027, as per ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. He has accumulated nearly $105 million in career earnings over 10 years with the Arizona Cardinals, as per Spotrac.A new team entered the trade discussion: the Jacksonville Jaguars. According to NFL analyst Bucky Brooks, the Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Philadelphia Eagles are potential trade destinations for Budda Baker.The veteran could help Jacksonville defend the run with his experience and physical approach. He brings leadership, physicality, and ball-hawking skills to the gridiron.The eight-time Pro Bowler could interest a squad looking to upgrade its playmaking potential in the secondary. The Arizona safety “is a valuable asset as a box-area defender built to play multiple spots in a three-safety scheme”, as per Bucky Brooks.As per ESPN’s Matt Bowen, Baker’s downhill speed and urgency to the ball make him a disruptive safety who can still play in split-field schemes or roam near the line of scrimmage. He is not a high-level playmaker in coverage [9 career interceptions], but he can defend the run, and his blitz adds impact to the game plan.
Article Summary: Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker has become one of the most popular names circulating in the NFL trade discussions. The 30-year-old safety’s three-year, $54 million contract makes him an unrestricted free agent in 2028; 2027 is his final year. Baker has not requested a trade or asked the Cardinals to keep him. Buffalo Bills, Jacksonville Jaguars, and Philadelphia Eagles are potential destinations for the veteran.

Article Title: Skin woes, nightly meds: Bittu Tabahi pays the price for his lonely crusade against public littering
Article Text:
​His parents are also worried about his health and have urged him to keep away from the river.

Poll Vote & Share your view Should schools incorporate environmental awareness into their curriculum? Definitely No, it's not necessary 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





BHOPAL: Surendra Singh Choudhary, the student and clean-up champion from Madhya Pradesh’s Biaora city, better known to his netizen followers as Bittu Tabahi, is literally paying the price for his lonely crusade against public littering.The second-year B.Sc student, who previously lamented repeated waste dumping in Ajnar river after every cleaning, urging greater public empathy and support, has developed persistent skin issues in his hands and legs. In fact, such is the severity of the pain and skin irritation that he has to depend on medication every night before sleep, his price for a waste-free Ajnar.Bittu set out on his solitary clean-up mission on Jan 26, 2026, removing plastic bottles, bags, algae and other waste from a clogged stretch of the Ajnar river, using basic tools and, at times, his bare hands. His effort soon got noticed, as before-after pictures and videos, attesting to his noble effort, went viral winning him global praise.However, the physical toll of his mission is now starting to tell on him, as Bittu said prolonged contact with contaminated water and waste has affected his skin, putting him in considerable discomfort.“The constant itching and pain in my hands and legs is causing me immense discomfort,” the 21-year-old told TOI, adding, “I have to take medicines every night before sleep, so I can wake up next morning and head back to the river.I know if I give up now, the waste will keep piling up on the river and all my effort will come to nought.”His parents are also worried about his health and have urged him to keep away from the river. Bittu, however, is determined to soldier on but would rather that his parents not know that he’s still involved in the river clean-up.“My parents are deeply concerned about my health,” he said, adding, “They don’t want me to enter the dirty waters and pick waste. This is why I haven’t told them that I am still involved in this effort and would rather keep it that way. I don’t want them to lose sleep worrying about me, but I also can’t bear to watch the river turning a dump time and time again.”Bittu’s concerns are not unfounded. After he spent months turning up tonnes of solid and plastic waste from the affected river stretch, reports came out in Oct about how plastic and other litter had begun accumulating again in the stretch he had restored.He said the river’s relapse into a dump was particularly heartbreaking as he had laboured without govt machinery, institutional funding or a formal campaign.“I did not take this initiative to win online praise. I did it as the river is built into our city’s character and identity and I couldn’t stand the sight of garbage accumulating on its waters. But when I see plastic and other kinds of litter being dumped again and again, it feels like all my hard work is going to waste,” Bittu told TOI.He had installed trash bins near the riverbank at his own expense to discourage dumping, but added that littering in the waters was continuing regardless.Despite the physical toll and emotional strain, Bittu said he will not abandon Ajnar. “My body is hurting, but my resolve is not defeated,” he said, adding, “As long as there is even a drop of waste, I will do everything in my power to remove it. My only request to the people is not to throw garbage in the waters. If people become more aware and give me the support I need, no student will have to risk his health cleaning these waters. ”While Bittu is not giving up yet, the enormity of his task demands far more than individual volunteerism. It calls for sustained municipal support, waste-management infrastructure and public awareness and involvement.
Article Summary: Bittu Tabahi, 21, has developed persistent skin issues in his hands and legs. His parents are also worried about his health and have urged him to keep away from the river. Bittu set out on his solitary clean-up mission on Jan 26, 2026.

Article Title: Mahatma Gandhi's grandson 30-acre Virginia land in US reclaimed after 20-month legal battle
Article Text:
Desai said he first visited the Virginia property in 2024 and commissioned a survey at a cost of $4,500.





SURAT: A US court has ordered a Virginia resident to remove his encroachment from land owned by the late Kanu Gandhi, Mahatma Gandhi’s grandson, and his wife Shiva Gandhi, after a 20-month legal battle led by Parimal Desai from Surat.The dispute involved 30 acres of land adjoining Shenandoah National Park in Warren County, Virginia, which the Gandhi couple bought in 1987. During their final years in South Gujarat, they created a charitable trust and transferred their assets to it. Desai now serves as managing trustee.Talking to TOI, Parimal Desai said, “It began when US national Gregory Black sent a legal notice to my residence on Jan 10, 2025. Black claimed the land by the adverse possession rule of Virginia, which allows a person to own land after 15 years of possession if five conditions are met. He ultimately could not prove his exclusive and actual possession condition and the ‘hostile claim’ condition.”Kanu Gandhi and Shiva Gandhi returned to India in 2013 and spent their final years in South Gujarat. Kanu Gandhi died in Surat in Nov 2016. Under his will, his assets passed to Shiva Gandhi.In 2018, Shiva Gandhi established ‘The Dr Schiva and Kanu Ramdas Mohandas Gandhi Charitable Trust’ and registered her will. After her death in 2020, the will was executed and Desai took charge as managing trustee. The trust inherited her properties and financial assets to support its charitable activities.Desai said he first visited the Virginia property in 2024 and commissioned a survey at a cost of $4,500.“As I learnt about the land in Virginia, I went to the property in 2024 and got the survey done. If the trust wanted to do anything with land, it had to be in its possession. I got the will probated in a US court in 2025 and got the land title in the trust’s name,” he said.Black claimed he had occupied the land since 2008. In court he cited trails, a cabin, tree stands, a culvert and other improvements on the property, along with photographs from to support his claim.Desai said, “I had hired lawyers in the US and worked in India to win the claim. I used artificial intelligence (AI) to find the ways to contest the claim. When the final trial took place, from Sep 8 to 11, I told the court that Kanu Gandhi was Mahatma Gandhi’s grandson and he and his wife has donated the properties to the trust, which has the objective of propagating Gandhian philosophy.“We could prove with GIS maps that the cabin was not there for 15 years. I also went there many times since 2020 which disproved his claim of actual possession. We also found another woman residing on the land, which belied Black’s claim that he had exclusive possession.”In the order dated Oct 21, Judge Daryl L. Funk of the Warren County Circuit Court ruled in favour of Desai and the trust. The court directed Black to pay $11,375 towards the fees of the Guardian ad Litem representing unknown heirs.The court also ordered Black to remove the cabin, hunting stands, hunting huts and personal belongings from the property within 30 days at his own expense. Black was directed to surrender possession of the land and cease entering or exercising any ownership rights over it.
Article Summary: Kanu Gandhi and Shiva Gandhi spent their final years in South Gujarat. Kanu Gandhi died in Surat in Nov 2016 and his assets passed to Shiva Gandhi. Shiva Gandhi established ‘The Dr Schiva and Kanu Ramdas Mohandas Gandhi Charitable Trust’ and registered her will in 2020. Parimal Desai took charge as managing trustee.

Article Title: '1st we lost our land, now compensation': Money from PNB’s Greater Noida branch accounts diverted to 6 accounts in Goa, Mumbai, Jharkhand
Article Text:
Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

30 complaints received, many claim gold & silver in locker replaced with faux jewellery

TOI

‘First we lost our land & now our compensation’

TOI





NOIDA: Money allegedly diverted from customers’ accounts at a Punjab National Bank (PNB) branch in Greater Noida reached six bank accounts in Goa, Mumbai and Jharkhand, police have found in their investigation into alleged embezzlement of Rs 35 crore from the branch. Police have frozen the accounts.The police cybercrime team and PNB’s vigilance team, investigating the alleged fraud, said the money didn’t stay in these accounts and have been routed to others. Investigators suspect that branch employees and the bank manager may have come into contact with a cyberfraud gang and allegedly facilitated the irregularities.So far, 30 account holders from Aichhar, Birondi, Bironda, Kyampur and several other neighbouring villages have submitted complaints at Beta 2 police station. The SHO said 12 fresh complaints were filed on Thursday and all the complaints were being clubbed into an FIR filed earlier under BNS Section 316(5) (criminal breach of trust) against the PNB branch staffers.The FIR was lodged on Wednesday after Shrichand, a resident of Viroondi Chakrasenpur village in Surajpur, alleged that Rs 1.16 crore was embezzled from his FD linked to his account at the Aichhar branch.On Thursday, several account holders staged a protest outside the Aichhar branch, with several claiming that gold and silver jewellery and other valuables have gone missing from lockers too.In some cases, these have been replaced with faux ornaments.Some accused bank officials of altering registered mobile numbers and email IDs before diverting money from fixed deposits (FDs) and savings accounts to ensure that account holders did not receive transaction alerts. Many complainants, most of them farmers who had received land compensation from Noida Authority, said their accounts were completely emptied out by the bank staff.Ajipal, a resident of Birondi village, toldthat he received compensation after his family’s land was acquired in 2001 and rented a locker at the bank in 2014. He said he learnt of the alleged fraud on Oct 27 and approached the bank for details on a Rs 35.34 lakh fixed deposit (FD) and 18 tolas (approximately 210 grams) of gold and 1 kg of silver jewellery in his locker, but the bank manager did not give a clear response. He alleged that the mobile number and email ID registered against his account did not match his actual contact details and may have been deliberately changed to stop him from receiving alerts about unauthorised transactions.“On Thursday, bank staffers were asking affected customers to submit affidavits detailing the money held in their fixed deposits (FDs) and the gold and silver jewellery kept in their lockers,” Ajipal said. While the process is meant to document their claims, several account holders said they were still awaiting clear answers about the status of their money and jewellery.Santosh, a resident from Birondi village, alleged that Rs 1.3 crore had been deposited in her bank account as land acquisition compensation, of which Rs 1.2 crore had allegedly gone missing. Expressing anguish over the alleged loss, she said her family had already lost its land to acquisition and had deposited the compensation money in the bank with the expectation that it would secure their future. “First, they took our land, and now the bank has taken away our compensation money,” she said.Meanwhile, senior bank officials from Mumbai and Noida, who have been called in to monitor the case, toldthat audits have been ordered at other branches in Gautam Budh Nagar where land acquisition compensation was deposited over the past two years. Rajesh Bhowmik, the bank’s zonal manager, said a case had been registered with the CBI. Money of three account holders has been credited to their accounts, he said. “…three claims amounting to Rs 43 lakh had been settled as of yesterday (Wednesday). The bank assures its customers that all genuine claims will be honoured,” PNB said in a statement.On Wednesday, PNB suspended the branch manager and four other employees. Bhowmik said the bank will examine each account holder’s case individually before refunding the amounts.“PNB has taken serious cognisance of the complaints regarding alleged financial irregularities involving certain customer fixed/ savings bank deposit accounts at its Greater Noida branch. The matter is being examined on priority, and the bank is extending full cooperation to the authorities concerned and is taking necessary steps to verify the facts, assess the extent of the reported discrepancies and address the concerns of affected customers,” the bank said in a statement.
Article Summary: 30 complaints received, many claim gold & silver in locker replaced with faux jewellery. Money allegedly diverted from customers’ accounts at a Punjab National Bank (PNB) branch in Greater Noida reached six bank accounts in Goa, Mumbai and Jharkhand. Police have frozen the accounts.

Article Title: BJP loses Darbhanga MLC seat to RJD in final stage of counting
Article Text:
RJD’s Anil Kumar Jha (right), who won Darbhanga Graduates’ seat, with party national working president Tejashwi Prasad Yadav





PATNA: The opposition RJD on Thursday won the Darbhanga Graduates’ constituency of the Bihar legislative council with its candidate Anil Kumar Jha defeating sitting MLC and BJP nominee Sarvesh Kumar after a dramatic shift in preferential votes during the final stage of counting.Officials at the counting centre at Khel Bhawan in Darbhanga told TOI Jha was declared elected after taking a lead of 533 votes over Kumar at the end of the 39th round, following the elimination of 38 candidates. A total of 40 candidates contested the seat, where polling was held on Oct 23.Darbhanga divisional commissioner-cum-returning officer Himanshu Kumar Rai told TOI over the phone Jha was declared elected on Thursday after completion of all formalities and receipt of the necessary approval from the Election Commission Until the end of the 38th round, the BJP candidate was ahead. Kumar had secured 20,033 votes, while Jha had polled 19,029, giving the BJP nominee a lead of 1,004 votes. The result changed in the 39th round after Mohammad Imtiyaz Noorani of Jan Suraaj, the third-leading candidate, was eliminated.Officials said voters who had marked Noorani as their first preference had also indicated second preferences for Kumar and Jha.Of these transferable votes, 2,900 went to Jha, while 1,363 were added to Kumar’s tally. The transfer gave Jha the decisive lead. With only the two leading candidates remaining in the count, the returning officer declared Jha elected.Kumar congratulated Jha at the counting centre soon after the result became clear.The outcome revised the final tally for the eight teachers’ and graduates’ constituencies that went to polls on Oct 23. The BJP won two seats, the RJD two, the JD(U) one, Jan Suraaj one and Independents two.BJP functionaries had on Wednesday claimed Kumar had retained the Darbhanga Graduates’ seat. However, counting continued till Thursday evening when the preference transfers altered the result.Reacting to the victory, RJD national working president Tejashwi Prasad Yadav said the Darbhanga Graduates’ verdict was “the educated society’s open mandate against the NDA govt’s corruption, abuse of power, BJP’s repressive action against teachers and youth, and the NDA’s anti-people policies.”
Article Summary: Opposition RJD wins Darbhanga Graduates’ constituency of Bihar legislative council. RJD candidate Anil Kumar Jha defeated sitting MLC and BJP nominee Sarvesh Kumar after a dramatic shift in preferential votes during the final stage of counting.

Article Title: After 34 years caring for a Crufts-winning breeder's dogs, a Hampshire kennel worker challenged her £1.1m will despite receiving £100,000; her son agreed to raise his monthly support from £350 to £850
Article Text:
Dog breeder (Representative image)

A life built around the kennels

The will and the claim

The son’s response

What the judge said

A dispute about more than money

A long-serving kennel worker who spent 34 years caring for prize-winning Airedale terriers has taken his late employer’s son to court over her £1.1m estate, arguing that the £100,000 left to him in her will was not enough to secure his future. The case has now led to an interim agreement under which the son will increase his monthly support from £350 to £850 while the dispute continues. The story, reported by The Independent, The Telegraph, The Times and the Daily Mail, centres on Mary Swash, a celebrated Hampshire breeder whose dogs achieved success at Crufts, and David Brand, the man who worked beside her for much of his adult life. Read more about it here:Mary Swash founded the Jokyl kennels in 1959 at her farm in West Tisted, near Alresford in Hampshire. Over the decades she became known internationally for breeding pedigree Airedale terriers, and her greatest show-ring triumph came in 1986 when her bitch, Ginger Christmas Carol, known at home as Emma, won Best in Show at Crufts.David Brand began living and working with Swash in 1992, when he was in his mid-twenties. He cared for her dogs, lived in accommodation on the farm and remained there after her death, looking after ten Airedales, six of which belong to her estate and four of which are his own.His lawyers told the High Court that he devoted his entire adult life to Swash’s kennels and that the arrangement was never simply an ordinary job.According to evidence heard in court, Swash provided Brand with his home, paid his bills, covered his food and vehicle costs and gave him £50 a week in pocket money. Her barrister said there was no formal employment contract and no conventional wage, describing the relationship instead as an informal arrangement that endured for 34 years. The judge, Deputy Master Michael Jefferis, accepted that this was not a commercial relationship and noted that Swash spoke of Brand as though he were family.Swash died aged 89 in July 2025. Her 2008 will, which was never changed, left Brand £100,000 and the remainder of her estate to her only son, John Cartledge. The estate consists mainly of the Hampshire farm, valued at £1.1m for probate in December, together with around £70,000 in cash.Brand later lodged a caveat freezing the estate’s assets and indicated that he would pursue a claim for reasonable financial provision under the Inheritance Act 1975. His case is that he was dependent on Swash and that she had promised to look after him for life. He also says he helped care for her during the final year of her life, alongside a professional carer.At a recent hearing in London’s High Court, Brand’s lawyers asked for either a £50,000 lump sum or £865 a month from the estate to support him until a full trial next year. They argued that he was in immediate need, had little money left and faced the winter while continuing to care for ten dogs. His counsel said the £300,000 accommodation offer made by Cartledge would not buy a suitable home in an expensive part of Hampshire, where Brand wished to remain.John Cartledge, Swash’s 63-year-old son and the executor of her estate, had already been paying Brand £350 a month. He was also providing food for the dogs and paying around £1,500 a month in estate expenses. In an email to Brand’s lawyers, he wrote that Brand would not be homeless and that he understood what he had meant to his mother, adding that it was his duty to ensure Brand lived comfortably for the rest of his life.Cartledge had also offered a more substantial settlement: buying Brand a £300,000 house with money from the estate, giving him the right to live there for life, on top of the £100,000 legacy. His lawyers argued that Brand’s claim could potentially consume the entire net value of the estate, leaving Cartledge with nothing from his mother’s will.After the hearing, however, Cartledge agreed to raise Brand’s monthly payments to £850, while continuing to meet around £1,500 a month in estate and dog-related expenses. The judge approved that undertaking, describing Cartledge as having been “quite generous” and saying he should be praised for recognising a responsibility to look after Brand.Deputy Master Jefferis found that Brand had a strong claim and an immediate need for support. He said the relationship between Swash and Brand was not merely that of employer and employee, pointing to the absence of a wage, the long-running informal arrangement and Swash’s stated hope that Brand would be settled in a house and looked after after her death.At the same time, the judge questioned whether £850 a month was perhaps on the generous side. He also asked why Brand could not seek other work, why caring for ten dogs should be treated as a full-time occupation, and why the dogs belonging to the estate could not be sold. Brand’s lawyers responded that the dogs were his companions and that rehoming them would be a cruel imposition on a man whose life had been built around them.The case is ultimately about how the law should treat someone who was neither a family member in the formal sense nor an ordinary employee. Brand received a significant legacy, but he argues that a lifetime of unpaid or loosely paid care, combined with dependence on Swash for housing and daily needs, justifies a greater share of her estate.For Cartledge, the dispute is equally personal. He maintains that he has tried to avoid court and has offered meaningful support, yet his lawyers say the claim now being advanced could leave him with no economic interest in the estate. The full trial is expected next year, when the court will decide whether Brand’s needs justify a larger provision from Swash’s £1.1m fortune.
Article Summary: David Brand worked at Mary Swash's kennels in Hampshire for 34 years. He was left £100,000 by her in her 2008 will, which was never changed. But he has taken her son, John Cartledge, 63, to court over the money. The case has now led to an interim agreement under which the son will increase his monthly support from £350 to £850 while the dispute continues.
